industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): financials and real estate investment trusts were the only sectors bought in the week (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct), Wood favours financials as the diversification from artificial intelligence, and Goldman (16 Oct) says Southern European banks are healthier than in 2011-15; against it, French spreads at decade highs with new spillover to Italy, the sovereign-bank loop. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, B prior. Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D.

sector.why: Neutral, carried unchanged, with Richard's question re-asked on this week's evidence. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the margin leg strengthened (financials among the only sectors bought, Jefferies desk 17 Oct; Wood favours financials; Southern European banks have healthier capital, asset quality and profitability than in 2011-15, Goldman 16 Oct; no non-performing loan cycle reported) and the sovereign leg worsened (French spreads at decade highs with tentative spillover to Italy, the loop that cut the row to Neutral); bank earnings and net interest margins were not read. Neither condition fired: French spreads are not under 100 basis points and no general European widening or default wave was read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, A prior. 20 of the 149 Pool stocks are banks; three sit in the top 40 of the starting score (ING Groep 2, ABN AMRO 24, Bank Polska Kasa Opieki 35). No memo carried a congruence line this week, so last week's four bank memos (one Congruent, three Mixed) stand. Counter-case unchanged on both sides; back to B on French spreads under 100 basis points, to D on a default wave or general European spread widening.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Overweight named and judged thin. Wilson (9-Oct) cites 'Ireland's turnaround' as the counter to euro-area sovereign stress, and the Bank of Ireland memo (Congruent) describes an Aa2 sovereign running a surplus at a 77% loan-to-deposit ratio. That is one strategist's clause and one memo on five stocks, so the row stays Neutral; moves to B if a second source names Ireland as the fiscal exception.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; medium conviction. Bank of Ireland (BIRG-IE) at 18.11 EUR (2026-10-09) is a sound business case and an insufficient investment case: the 'Modal return' on the modal path is 9.3 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.0 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar, because the shares stand at 8.7 times 24-month-forward earnings, the 86th percentile of their own five-year range, with the sector moved from Overweight to Neutral in the week of 2026-10-09. The park is on the return, not on the gate: no D or F sits on management, business quality, predictability or trackability. Two re-entry triggers, either of which turns the case bullish with the business case unchanged: a price near 15.75 EUR (the level at which the modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months), or evidence that the discount to AIB is closing (FY2026 capital generation above 270 basis points with a buyback above 600 EUR millions and the price-to-earnings gap to AIB inside 5 percent). The primary 'Target Setup' is 'Compounder' at a C fit; the secondary is 'Major Corporate Change' at C.
case: - The thesis in the record's words: Bank of Ireland is a capital-return case with a contracted earnings tailwind, in a consolidated home market, bought at a price that already pays for most of it. The bank probably earns what the market expects, and the market has already paid for it.

- The change that drives the thesis is internal and mechanical, and it is already in the financial statements. The structural hedge rolls off swaps written near 1.14 percent into swaps averaging about 2.79 percent on about 70 to 77 EUR billions, enlarged by 8 EUR billions in July 2026 (which cut net interest income sensitivity by about 30 percent to 185 EUR millions per 100 basis points lower); management guides net interest income from c. 3.5 EUR billions in FY2026 to 3.75 in FY2027 and above 3.95 in FY2028. Net interest income troughed in H2 2025 after falling 9 percent from FY2023 to FY2025; H1 2026's 1,705 EUR millions is flat on the half and the turn is guided for three years. Deutsche Bank notes the hedge was added as rates peaked, somewhat pro-cyclical, and yields 1.9 percent against AIB's 2.4: the drag now is the tailwind later.

- The internal forces meet the screen's rule: three strong (guidance raised A: four FY2026 lines raised on 31 July 2026 and FY2028 targets raised in March 2026; shareholder returns A: the interim up 56 percent, the fifth year of buybacks; balance-sheet utilisation A: the hedge addition and the bond book to 23.0 EUR billions) and three moderate (strategy C: Strategy 2028 a continuation with 1.5 EUR billions of investment and the US Leveraged Acquisition Finance exit as the one decisive choice; standards B: 41 EUR millions of savings in H1 2026 against 250 by 2028, headcount down 3 percent, artificial intelligence to deliver 20 percent of the programme; perimeter C: the non-core books to 1.2 EUR billions, under 2 percent of a loan book of roughly 83 EUR billions). The red-flag check is clean except the 71 EUR millions reclassification. No chief-executive change (D as an absent force: Myles O'Grady since late 2022); no new geographies (D). Internal forces B; not A because each force is a continuation of the 2023-25 cycle run faster.
counter_case: - At its strongest, the reading the risks research calls a 'false friend': the H1 2026 beat was built on things that do not recur, and behind it the bank is a rate-cycle beneficiary at a plateau, bought at the top of its own range in the week its sector lost its Overweight. The 15 percent profit-before-tax beat rested on impairment write-backs, a cost of risk of 8 basis points against a normal 20 to 25, 30 EUR millions of insurance benefit in the impairment line, and a 39c interim dividend 26 percent above consensus; none is a run rate. The net interest margin is 2.68 percent, down from 3.03 in 2023, and the structural hedge yields 1.9 percent on 66 EUR billions against AIB's 2.4 on 75, a drag of 12 to 20 percent on reported net interest income. The deposit franchise is about to be arbitraged by licensed neobanks with local IBANs and 3.5 percent savings yields; the digital offering is a poor second to AIB after 1.4 EUR billions of spend; the UK book is retreating with new lending down 22 percent; the motor finance tail is up to 950 EUR millions on RBC's reading against 429 provided. All of it bought at the 86th percentile of the five-year range, with Deutsche Bank removing the stock from its top picks on 8 September 2026. The forward estimates are right and the price is wrong; the price corrects first through the multiple when the rate or credit cycle turns, as Morgan Stanley's 10.50 EUR bear value (a 12 percent return on tangible equity at 0.8 times tangible book) describes, minus 42 percent from its base.

- The record concedes: the H1 2026 cost of risk is not a run rate (its path doubles it by FY2026 and triples it by FY2029); the net interest income guidance is in consensus and no upgrade remains on that line; the digital lag and the pay cap are real and slow to fix; the multiple is at the top of its own range and the sector's momentum has turned; and the return at the modal multiple does not clear the bar, the point on which the counter-case and the record agree.
triggers: - Re-entry trigger one: a price near 15.75 EUR, at which the modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months (about 14.00 EUR on the three-year test).

- Re-entry trigger two: evidence the discount to AIB is closing, read as FY2026 capital generation above 270 basis points with a buyback above 600 EUR millions and the price-to-earnings gap to AIB inside 5 percent; towards the de-rating branch, the ten-year 75th percentile of 8.90 times lost on the way down with the sector.

- The net interest income path: the record's side is probable, about 70 percent, that net interest income lands within 3 percent of 3.5 / 3.75 / above 3.95 EUR billions; changes its mind on an ECB rate at or below 2.00 percent with the FY2027 guidance cut below 3.5 EUR billions; alarm at a guidance cut below 3.65.

- The deposit franchise: probable, about 65 percent, that the term mix stays at or below 14 percent and current-account outflows below 1.0 EUR billion in any half through FY2028; changes its mind on a half-year term flow above 1.0 EUR billion, the earnings review's own invalidation trigger; a Revolut Irish mortgage launch is the step that would move the shares, the wrong way.

- Costs: plausible, about 60 percent, that FY2027 operating costs stay at or below 2.3 EUR billions; changes its mind on FY2026 costs above 2.3 EUR billions or the mid-40s cost-to-income target withdrawn; the 2.2 against 2.0 EUR billions cost figures are unreconciled.

- Credit including conduct: probable, about 65 percent, that the annualised cost of risk stays at or below 25 basis points in every year to FY2028; changes its mind above 40 basis points or on a motor finance top-up above 500 EUR millions; the drop-through sensitivity shows a 10 percent earnings miss from the lines below pre-provision profit turns the D into an F.
